![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/4de50fc0b2b2f05b9ca60e28ffc65900a2b0780549fbf1cf32150a903a08faf5.png)

The scatter plot above gives the correspondence between the variables $x$ and $y$ for some data points.
Use the trend line to predict the value of $x$ when $y=20.$
question.worked_solution:
To make our prediction, we proceed as follows:

- First, we start at $y=20$ on the $y$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/b614a0ed708e9b0e333c05daf6adde3f4636daebf00f622fc570ade99d8237d8.png)

- Then, we move right until we intersect the trend line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/d6772acc92fc6b1ed7c9efbeb4a292ec21f5d2b8069bd0fa4ad7a8d5f7d79470.png)

- Finally, we move down until we intersect the $x$-axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/3916c8c4a6bfa6cb558cfa91e268e66d011659753ca23da0396cf2ed9f8d1a8f.png)

Therefore, when $y=20,$ we obtain $x≈7.$
